My pick is the **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2,048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station"/>**. It offers the best combination of actual RV compatibility, battery capacity, output power, and sale price in the supplied results.

<badge color="success">Best overall RV pick</badge> <badge color="success">Under $900</badge>

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="124px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **BLUETTI AC200L**

    <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" lineThrough={true} size="sm">$899.00 regular price</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">BLUETTI Official US Store · In stock according to supplied results</text>
    **Promo code:** `AFF5OFF`

    <Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="Buy BLUETTI AC200L — discounted link"/>
  </box>
</row>

### Why I recommend it

| Specification | BLUETTI AC200L |
|---|---:|
| Battery capacity | 2,048Wh |
| Battery chemistry | LiFePO4 |
| AC output | 2,400W |
| RV outlet | Built-in TT-30 (30A plug) |
| Solar input | 1,200W |
| Regular price | $899 |
| Discounted price | **$854.05** |

The biggest advantage is its built-in TT-30 RV outlet. You can connect your RV shore-power cable directly without needing an additional adapter setup.

### Other contenders

Based on the supplied comparison results:

| Model | Capacity | AC output | Price | Main advantage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | **$854.05** | RV-focused choice |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | 2,048Wh | — | $899.99 | Lighter, 41.7 lb |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | 1,612Wh | 3,000W | $799 | High output |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $676.16 | Best budget value |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | 2,048Wh | 2,500W | $699 | Excellent price |

Source: supplied search results, including Dealectric and GearRanking. <Cite refs={["turn428731view0"]}/>

### Three important RV considerations

1. **Don't assume the TT-30 outlet delivers 30A continuously.** The AC200L's 2,400W inverter provides approximately 20A at 120V. It can run refrigerators, lights, water pumps and coffee makers, but isn't sufficient to run a typical rooftop RV air conditioner reliably.

2. **Manage your RV converter.** It can charge your RV house battery, but consumes power from the station. Turn it off once the house battery is full.

3. **Use propane for a two-way refrigerator.** Running it on AC electricity can consume 2.4–3.6kWh daily, exceeding the AC200L's entire battery capacity.

<Cite refs={["turn428731view0"]}/>

One caveat: the AC200L is an older model, and BLUETTI Canada lists it as discontinued. The supplied results report US-store availability on October 31, 2026, so I'd verify stock and warranty before purchasing.

### My final verdict

- **Best RV-specific choice:** BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05.
- **Best budget alternative:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16.
- **Best if portability matters:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2.

I'd choose the BLUETTI if your priority is plugging directly into your RV and powering everyday appliances without spending more than $900.
